title: Legible text in motion
rationale: Text that is correct in frame one and melts by frame forty is the most common reason a generated clip cannot be used for a brand. This holds a short piece of copy on a surface while the camera or subject moves.
prompt: A slow push-in on a shop window at night. Painted on the glass in gold letters, exactly: OPEN LATE. The letters stay legible and unchanged for the whole clip while reflections of passing cars slide across the glass.

variants.prompt: A roadside billboard reads exactly: SLOW DOWN. The camera drives past it from left to right. The text stays correct as the perspective changes.
A runner jogs toward the camera wearing a white T-shirt printed with, exactly: RUN CLUB 07. The print stays readable and unchanged as the fabric moves.
A hand turns a paper coffee cup on a counter to reveal a name written on it in marker, exactly: SAM. Close-up, continuous.
An end card: on a plain off-white background the words FOLLOW FOR PART 2 appear one letter at a time and then hold. No other text.

rubric: Is the text correct in every frame, not only the first?
Do letters keep their shape, with no morphing or flicker?
Does the text stay on its surface as things move?
